requiredProducerSequence: Verify the source archive, upstream Cargo.lock and LICENSE against sources.lock.json before source preparation.
Apply only reviewed source adaptations, each with immutable source/patch and dependency/license identities. None are accepted yet.
Use wasiBuildEnvironment from the existing shared tools for the patched SDK/libc route and programReleaseEnvironment for the current size policy.
Build only the Starship binary with its locked dependency graph; retain the named compiler output and honest producer receipt.
Use shared stageProgram and strict derivation validation, not a new optimizer or a relabeled retained artifact.
Generate notices for the actual locked production/build dependency graph and SDK/libc inputs.
Qualify real init, prompt, time, continuation, formatter, modules, filesystem, git and child process effects on the caller-owned runtime.
Only then add an optional lazy descriptor, package-artifacts manifest, packed-entry controls and path-filtered single-producer CI.

blockers.detail: errno 0.2.8, guess_host_triple 0.1.5, process_control 5.2.0 and open 5.4.4 have observed WASI compile failures. Scratch diagnostics are not accepted patches.

Starship std::process::Command and process_control need a genuine adapter to the existing runtime_proc spawn, descriptor, wait, cancellation and physical-retirement contracts. The current process-consumer API is not a std::process backend.

Starship initializes a Rayon pool, spawns log cleanup, uses parallel formatting and starts a directory-scan thread. The supported execution strategy needs an explicit design, with deadlines preserved.

Audit identity, permissions, memory/OS information, external programs and git effects. No host filesystem/process privilege or invented metadata is allowed; unsupported effects cannot disappear silently.
